> Initial read: signs point to a dedicated GPU pool headroom exhaustion plus token-queue buildup on a few hot routes (predict-text).

Checked dp-42 telemetry and kernel traces:
- GPU utilization: ~98% across the pool (sustained for ~35m).
- Async queue depth for predict-text up ~6x baseline; KV cache hit-rate unchanged.
- Several long-running generation sessions (seq len spikes) are blocking batching windows.
- Observed elevated kernel swap/recompile messages for optimized attention kernels on 2 nodes — likely caused by mixed model variants that recently rolled.

Short-term mitigation (actionable in next 10–20m):
1) Push a route-level fallback for rerank -> model: rwd-opt-2b-quant (lighter, compatible) — reduces token compute by ~60%.
2) Temporarily enable per-tenant request shaping on ClearCrest's key to cap burst QPS (recommended cap: current_qps * 0.75).
3) Evict a few long-lived sessions (notify users) to free batch windows — we can target sessions >120s.
4) Request a short-term reserved throughput bump (ops-concession) for dp-42 while we rebalance pools.

I'll push steps 1 and 2 now and post back with telemetry. Attaching quick snapshot: (attachment: clearcrest_pool_trace_20261002.txt)
